set.body:
Objective:
Turn the current one-way layering into a clean capability composition boundary. Preserve scala-slurm ownership of scheduler mechanics and evidence; preserve Sojourn ownership of compute-site, data-plane, batch/pool, and lease semantics; remove duplicated task, lifecycle, and filesystem machinery.

Scope:
1. Extract a scheduler-neutral shared contract and filesystem kernel.
2. Establish one operation descriptor and registry model.
3. Replace SlurmSite shadow lifecycle state with an injected managed batch executor.
4. Return a verified payload from result attachment without rereading or redecoding.
5. Derive local CLI and SSH constructors from one capability-based Slurm interpreter.

Completion criteria:
- All five child items are closed with their focused acceptance evidence.
- Dependency graphs for both repositories are acyclic and show no sojourn-core dependency on scala-slurm-core or scala-slurm-worker.
- The public Sojourn SPI exposes no scheduler-specific operation, transport, or package-owned implementation type.
- There is one authoritative operation identity, retry provenance, result validation path, and durable batch lifecycle source of truth.
- Pool policy remains in Sojourn; scheduler submission, observation, accounting, and transport remain in scala-slurm.
- scala-slurm formatting, tests, cross-build/package gates, and local evidence gate pass.
- Sojourn formatting and full test suite pass, including local Store, Batch, Pool, and Parity TCK laws plus Slurm batch acceptance on the disposable or configured controller.
- Architecture docs include the final dependency diagram, capability ownership table, migration notes, and explicitly documented remaining limitations.

Review rule:
No child closes on compile success alone. Each must include source evidence, focused behavioral tests, and repository-wide gates proportional to the changed boundary.
set.title: SCOMP: Make Sojourn and scala-slurm cleanly compositional
